subject: general
question: What is the ratio between times taken by a train 240 m long to cross an electric pole and a bridge of 80 m length?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the speed of a train is constant, the time taken is directly proportional to the distance covered.

Distance to cross a pole = Length of the train = 240 m

Distance to cross the bridge = Length of the train + Length of the bridge = 240 + 80 = 320 m

Ratio of times = Ratio of distances = 240 : 320 = 3 : 4

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the train = 240 m

Length of the bridge = 80 m

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

 
 Crossing an Electric Pole
 
 Train (240 m)
 
 
• 
 Pole
 
• 
 Distance = 240 m

 
 Crossing a Bridge
 
 Train (240 m)
 
 Bridge (80 m)
 
• 
 Total Distance = 320 m

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the train be v m/s.

⇒ Time taken to cross the electric pole (T₁) = Length of train ÷ Speed

⇒ T₁ = 240 ÷ v

⇒ Total distance covered to cross the bridge = Length of train + Length of bridge

⇒ Total distance = 240 + 80 = 320 m

⇒ Time taken to cross the bridge (T₂) = Total distance ÷ Speed

⇒ T₂ = 320 ÷ v

⇒ Ratio of times = T₁ : T₂ = (240 ÷ v) : (320 ÷ v)

⇒ Ratio = 240 : 320

⇒ Ratio = 3 : 4

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Crossing a Point Object

When a train crosses a stationary object of negligible length (like a pole, standing man, or signal post), the total distance covered is exactly equal to the length of the train.

Crossing a Platform or Bridge

When a train crosses an object with measurable length (like a bridge, platform, or another train), the total distance covered is the sum of the train's length and the object's length.

Relative Speed Rules

If two trains move in opposite directions, their relative speed = S₁ + S₂. If they move in the same direction, their relative speed = S₁ − S₂.
